title: TermAl cannot report which build it is running, nor which UI bundle it serves
outcome:
You cannot ask a running TermAl which build it is. /api/health returns only {ok, serverInstanceId} and there is no route that reports a commit, a build time, or a UI bundle identity. Grepping src for a build/version route finds only CARGO_PKG_VERSION echoed inside the ACP, Codex-RPC and delegation-MCP protocol handshakes - a package version that does not change between commits and is not exposed to an operator at all.

CONCRETE CASE, measured 2026-09-08 23:3x, three different versions in play at once on this machine:
- Served UI bundle: assets/index-Bsg3TWqz.js, built 2026-09-07 01:03 from commit 829d832.
- Running server binary: target/release/termal.exe, mtime 2026-09-07 22:19, launched 22:55 as `cargo run --release` (PID 15284, child PID 59664). The newest commit before that build time is 4dec5eb.
- Repository HEAD: 511cd20, 2026-09-08 10:55, one large commit ahead of the binary.

The binary's identity there is INFERRED from mtime against the commit timeline. It is not proof: the tree could have been dirty at build time, and nothing in the process or the API can settle it. That inability is the issue.

WHY IT MATTERS OPERATIONALLY, not theoretically: the decision in front of us tonight is which UI bundle to deploy, and the correct answer depends on which commit the RUNNING BINARY corresponds to, because a UI newer than its backend can call endpoints that do not exist yet. Right now that question can only be answered by reading file timestamps and reasoning about a commit log. A deploy decision should not rest on an inference from an mtime.

MINIMUM USEFUL SHAPE: a read-only endpoint reporting the commit the binary was built from, whether that tree was dirty, the build time, and the identity of the UI bundle currently being served - plus the same values surfaced where an operator will actually look. Engram has this modelled in its own identity slices; TermAl has nothing equivalent for itself, which is the gap.
